answer: Admission necessitates 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard work to register, a constraint acting as a technical oasis against sybil floods. The verifier enforces this by mandating a non-parallelizable buffer for computation, ensuring that any attempt to simulate multiple identities is caught like a prism refracting light into distinct, traceable paths. An honest agent pays 1,000 units of work, whereas an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes incurs a 1,000,000 unit cost; a fable of zero-refund policy maintains strict order. No identities are transferable.
